sentences.text: Dalpiazia is a member of the family Sclerorhynchidae, a group of extinct marine reptiles.
The genus was established by Checchia-Rispoli in 1933, with Dalpiazia stromeri serving as the type species.
The defining fossil for this species is surprisingly just a single rostral tooth.
This specific tooth was named in 1933 to honor the paleontologist Ernst Stromer.
These animals lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
Remains have been recovered from Maastrichtian rocks in mines across Jordan, Libya, Morocco, and Syria.
Scientists debate whether Dalpiazia is a valid genus, as it shares strong similarities with Ischyrhiza, a subgenus of Onchosaurus.
